components.note: 石 (stone) shows hard things knocking together.
並 (bìng) gives a rough sound hint; the traditional right part is the sound side.

example.english: I ran into my teacher on the road.
example.fact: 碰 means to bump or touch lightly and, with 到, to meet by chance: 碰到 / 碰见 (run into). It also appears in 碰运气 (to try one's luck) and 碰杯 (to clink glasses).

components.note: 林 (woods) is the upper part, standing for the shape of eyes closing in the simplified form.
夕 (evening) is the lower part and places the dream at night.

example.pinyin: Wǒ zuówǎn zuòle yí gè mèng.
example.english: I had a dream last night.
example.fact: 梦 pairs with the verb 做: 做梦 (to dream). It also means a hope or ideal: 梦想 (dream, aspiration), 美梦 (sweet dream) and 噩梦 (nightmare). 梦 is also the first character of 红楼梦, Dream of the Red Chamber.

components.note: 氵 (water) shows flowing, rolling water.
衮 (gǔn) gives the sound exactly.

example.pinyin: Qiú gǔn dào zhuōzi xiàmiàn qù le.
example.english: The ball rolled under the table.
example.fact: 滚 is literally 'to roll' (滚动), and 'to boil' in 水滚了. As an imperative, 滚! means 'get lost!', which is very rude, so use it carefully; 滚蛋 is a similar curse.

components.note: Built from a head-wear shape and 戈 (a spear-axe); the original sense is putting something on the head and carrying it.

example.fact: 戴 is the verb for putting on things worn on the head, face or hands: 戴帽子, 戴眼镜 (glasses), 戴手表 (a watch), 戴戒指 (a ring). Clothes use 穿, so 戴 and 穿 are a classic pair for learners.

components.note: Picture of a baby with a big head, arms stretched out and legs bound in swaddling.

example.fact: 子 is mostly a noun suffix pronounced neutral-tone zi: 桌子 (table), 椅子 (chair), 孩子 (child). On its own, zǐ means child or son and appears in titles like 孔子 (Confucius) and 君子 (gentleman).

components.note: 艹 (grass) is the top part and suggests hiding behind plants.
臧 (zāng) gives the sound; the finals are the same.

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ qián cáng zài chuáng xià.
example.english: He hid the money under the bed.
example.fact: 藏 has two readings: cáng ('to hide', as here) and zàng ('storehouse; Tibet', as in 西藏 and 宝藏). 藏 is the verb in the game 捉迷藏 (hide and seek).

components.note: 广 (a building) shows a shelter, with the idea of a base.
氐 (dǐ) gives the sound exactly.

example.pinyin: Bēizi de dǐ shì hóngsè de.
example.english: The bottom of the cup is red.
example.fact: 底 is 'bottom' or 'base': 海底 (sea floor), 底下 (underneath), 到底 (in the end, 'on earth' for questions) and 年底 (year's end). 到底 is a typical emphatic question word, as in 你到底想要什么？

components.note: 忄 (heart) shows feelings.
青 (qīng) gives the sound; the final differs slightly.

example.english: He is a very sentimental person.
example.fact: 情 is a bound form for emotions and circumstances: 爱情 (love), 友情 (friendship), 事情 (matter) and 情况 (situation). 事情 'matter, thing' is a common word that leans on this sense.

components.note: 夫 (a man) appears twice, one replacing another.
日 (sun) is the lower part, and also appears to give a loose sound hint.

example.fact: 替 works as a verb ('replace') and as a preposition 'for/on behalf of': 替我谢谢他 ('thank him for me'). It differs from 给 (gěi), which shows the receiver, whereas 替 shows the person you act in place of.

components.note: Picture of a face outline with an eye or nose inside it, a simple image of a head's front.

example.english: The surface of the table is very clean.
example.fact: 面 means face, surface and side: 前面 (front), 外面 (outside), 见面 (to meet face to face) and 面子 (face, social prestige). 面 is also the character for noodles (面条) in mainland usage, a different word with the same shape.

components.note: Shape is a lid-like stroke over 八; the number was borrowed and the parts do not explain its meaning, so learn it as a whole.

example.fact: 六 is considered lucky in Chinese culture because it sounds like 溜 ('smooth'), as in the saying 六六大顺 ('smooth sailing'). It also appears in 六一 (Children's Day, June 1).

components.note: Simplified from 飛, which showed a bird with outstretched wings flapping; the modern shape is a short curved line with two flicks.

example.fact: 飞 is to fly and to go quickly: 飞机 (airplane), 飞行 (flight), 起飞 (take off), and 飞快 (very fast). People also say 飞 casually for 'go by plane': 我明天飞北京.

components.note: Picture of rising vapour as three wavy lines, the cloud of breath in the air.

example.fact: 气 is an important concept: air (空气), weather (天气), breath, energy (the Daoist qi) and anger (生气). 别客气 ('you're welcome', 'don't be so polite') is a very common phrase.

components.note: 冫 (ice, here a water radical) hints at water.
中 (zhōng) gives the sound; the finals are close.

example.fact: 冲 has the readings chōng ('to rush, to flush, to rinse', as in 冲茶, 冲凉) and chòng ('towards, facing', as in 冲着). 冲 is used for brewing tea or coffee with hot water: 冲咖啡.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) marks a body part.
却 (què) gives a rough sound hint.

example.fact: 脚 is the foot, as opposed to 腿 (leg): 脚趾 (toe), 脚步 (footstep) and 脚印 (footprint). The measure word is 只 for one foot and 双 for a pair.

components.note: 殳 (a hand with a tool) shows a striking action.
臼 (a mortar) is the thing being struck.

example.fact: 毁 is a formal verb for destroying: 毁坏 (damage), 毁灭 (destroy), 毁容 (disfigure) and 毁约 (break a contract). It's used for things that can't easily be repaired, unlike 弄坏.

components.note: 大 (big) is the top part.
镸 (long) is the lower part, a long piece of cloth that wraps it.

example.pinyin: Wǒ mǎile yí tào xīn yīfu.
example.english: I bought a new set of clothes.
example.fact: 套 is a measure word for sets (一套房子, 一套工具), and a verb for putting a cover on: 套上 (put on), 手套 (gloves) and 外套 (coat). It also forms 套路 (routine, or a formula) and 客套 (polite formalities).

components.note: 口 (two mouths) at the top show wailing.
犬 (dog) at the bottom suggests a howling sound.

example.pinyin: Bié kū le, méi shì le.
example.fact: 哭 is to cry audibly, whereas 流泪 is 'to shed tears' and 眼泪 is the tears. Phrases like 哭笑不得 ('not know whether to laugh or cry') are common.

components.note: Simplified from 畫, which showed a hand holding a brush drawing the borders of a field; the modern form keeps the field 田 inside a frame.

example.pinyin: Tā zài huà yì zhī māo.
example.fact: 画 is both verb and noun: 画画儿 (draw), 一幅画 (a painting), 画家 (painter). 画 is also the stroke of a character in 笔画 (strokes), so 'how many strokes' is 几画.

components.note: 疒 (sickness) marks an illness.
丙 (bǐng) gives the sound; the tones differ.

example.fact: 病 is illness: 生病 (to get sick), 看病 (see a doctor), 病人 (patient) and 病毒 (virus). 病 can also be a fault: 语病 means 'a grammar error'.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread) shows a string.
戋 (jiān) gives the sound; the finals are close.

example.fact: 线 is thread, line or wire, and also route: 线路 (circuit, route), 电线 (cable), 在线 (online) and 路线 (route). 在线 is the standard word for 'online'.

components.note: ⺌ (flames) is the top, showing fire.
儿 (a person) is the base, so the character shows a person holding fire, giving light.

example.fact: 光 is light, as in 阳光 (sunshine), 月光 and 光明. It also means 'only' or 'used up': 光吃饭 (just eating), 吃光 (eat it all up). 光 can describe a smooth surface too: 光滑.

components.note: 礻 (altar) shows religion.
申 (shēn) gives the sound exactly.

example.fact: 神 is god, spirit and mind: 神仙 (immortal), 神话 (myth), 精神 (spirit, vigour) and 神秘 (mysterious). As an adjective in slang, 神 means amazing: 神奇.

components.note: 扌 (hand) shows grasping.
喿 (zào) gives the sound; the finals are close.

example.fact: 操 means to grasp, drill or exercise: 体操 (gymnastics), 早操 (morning exercises), 操作 (operate) and 操心 (to worry about). The very rude word 操 is a vulgar slang, so avoid it in everyday talk.

components.note: 辶 (walking) shows going along a path.
首 (shǒu) gives the sound; the finals are close, and it also means 'head', so leading the way.

example.fact: 道 is a road and a way, and the root of 道理 (reason), 知道 (know), 道歉 (apologise) and 道德 (morals). It is also the Dao (道) of Daoism. In classical or opera speech it means 'to say'.

components.note: 扌 (hand) shows pressing.
安 (ān) gives the sound exactly.

example.fact: 按 is to press, and as a preposition it means 'according to': 按时 (on time), 按照 (in accordance with), 按钮 (button). 按摩 is massage.

components.note: 勹 (a wrapping shape) is the outer cover.
巳 (a baby) is the contents inside, so the character shows swaddling a baby.

example.fact: 包 means to wrap (包饺子), and as a noun it's a bag or package: 书包, 钱包 (wallet), 面包 (bread) and 包子 (steamed bun). It's also a measure word for packs: 一包烟.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) marks a body part.
退 (tuì) gives the sound; the finals are the same.

example.fact: 腿 is the leg, from thigh to foot: 大腿 (thigh), 小腿 (calf), 腿疼 (leg ache). Food terms use it too: 鸡腿 (chicken drumstick) and 火腿 (ham).

components.note: Picture of a nose, since people in China point to their nose to refer to themselves.

example.fact: 自 is a bound form meaning 'self': 自己 (oneself), 自由 (freedom), 自然 (nature), 自信 (self-confidence), and 'from' in 来自 (come from). Its shape is the nose, and a person pointing at their nose means themselves.

components.note: 攵 (a hand with a stick) shows the idea of arranging by force.
敕 (chì) gives the shape of 束 and 正 together; the sound link is loose.

example.pinyin: Wǒ děngle zhěngzhěng yí gè xiǎoshí.
example.fact: 整 means whole and also neat: 整个 (the whole), 整齐 (tidy), 整理 (to sort out) and 整天 (all day). In dialect, 整 also means 'to do' or 'to mess with': 整人 (play a trick on someone).

components.note: 口 (mouth) suggests speaking what one knows.
矢 (shǐ, arrow) is the left part and gives a rough sound hint.

example.fact: 知 on its own is formal. The everyday verb is 知道, 'to know a fact'. Compounds include 通知 (notice), 知识 (knowledge) and 无知 (ignorant). It is different from 认识, which means to know a person.

components.note: 覀 (flames over a cover) is the upper part.
示 (altar) is the lower part, from an old image of burning paper offerings at an altar.

example.fact: 票 takes the measure word 张 and covers tickets (车票, 门票), votes (投票) and bills (钞票). It's also used for a 'ticket' in the sense of a pass: 机票 (plane ticket).

components.note: 纟 (silk thread) shows weaving threads together.
且 (qiě) gives a loose sound hint.

example.fact: 组 is to form and a group: 小组 (team), 组织 (organise), 组成 (be made up of), 组合 (combination). In Chinese schools, a 小组 is a study group.

components.note: 灬 (fire) shows light.
昭 (zhāo) gives the sound exactly.

example.english: Please do it according to this method.
example.fact: 照 means to shine, to take a photo (照相) and 'according to' (照着). 照片 is a photo, 照顾 means to look after and 护照 is a passport.

components.note: Picture of a person with crossed legs, which gives the idea of crossing and meeting.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zuòyè jiāo gěi lǎoshī.
example.english: Please hand in your homework to the teacher.
example.fact: 交 means to hand over, to cross and to make friends: 交作业, 交钱 (pay), 交朋友 and 交通 (traffic). 交 is a classic action word for 'hand in' tasks.

components.note: A vertical stroke crossed by a horizontal one; originally a single vertical line stood for ten.

example.fact: 十 is a simple cross and also stands for 'complete' in idioms: 十全十美 means 'perfect in every way'. For tens, 十一 is 11, and 二十 is 20.

components.note: Built from 厶 over 口; the parts do not clearly explain the meaning of 'platform', so it is best learned as a whole.

example.fact: 台 is a platform or stage, as in 舞台, 电视台 (TV station) and 台风 (typhoon). It's also the measure word for machines and shows (一台电脑) and the short name for Taiwan (台湾).

components.note: 扌 (hand) shows moving by hand.
般 (bān) gives the sound exactly.

example.fact: 搬 means to move bulky things from one place to another: 搬家 (move house), 搬东西 (carry things) and 搬运 (transport). It's used for moving objects, whereas 移 is more abstract.

components.note: 木 (wood) shows the material of old buildings.
娄 (lóu) gives the sound exactly.

example.english: I live on the third floor.
example.fact: 楼 is a multi-storey building and a floor number: 五楼 (5th floor), 楼上 (upstairs), 楼梯 (staircase) and 大楼 (building). In Chinese, ground floor is 一楼, as in American usage.

components.note: 尸 (a body or room) is the outer frame.
口 (mouth) inside it suggests discussion in a confined space.

example.english: We played a game of chess.
example.fact: 局 is a bureau or office (邮局, post office; 公安局, police station), a situation (局面) and a measure word for a round of a game (一局棋). 结局 means 'ending' of a story.

components.note: 目 (eye) shows the organ.
艮 (gèn) gives the sound; only the initial differs.

example.fact: 眼 is the eye, usually as 眼睛; it also counts glances (看一眼 'take a look') and small holes (泉眼). 眼 appears in 眼镜 (glasses) and 眼泪 (tears).

components.note: Picture of flames with tongues of fire rising from a base.

example.fact: 火 is fire and also 'popular': 火车 (train, literally 'fire cart'), 火山 (volcano), 生火 (light a fire). In slang, 火 means 'hot, trendy', as in 这首歌很火. In Chinese medicine, 上火 is 'too much internal heat'.

components.note: 犭 (animal) shows that this is an animal.
苗 (miáo) gives the sound; it matches the cat's miaow.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu yì zhī māo.
example.fact: 猫 takes the measure word 只 (一只猫). It forms 熊猫 (panda, literally 'bear cat'), 小猫 (kitten) and 猫咪 (kitty, cute). The phrase 招财猫 is the lucky waving cat.

components.note: 上 (above) sits on top.
卜 (a stick) is below; the shape reads as something wedged, which suits the sense of being stuck.

example.english: I didn't bring my bank card.
example.fact: 卡 is borrowed from English 'card' as in 银行卡, 信用卡 and 卡片. It's also used for 'to be stuck': 卡住 (get stuck), and in slang 很卡 means a laggy device. Sometimes it's read qiǎ (to block), as in 关卡.

components.note: 氵 (water) shows washing.
先 (xiān) gives the sound; the initial is the same and the final differs slightly.

example.english: I need to wash my hands.
example.fact: 洗 is to wash: 洗手, 洗脸, 洗澡 (bathe), 洗衣服, 洗碗 (wash dishes). It also appears in 洗手间 (restroom) and 洗发水 (shampoo).

components.note: 氵 (water) shows liquids mixing together.
昆 (kūn) gives the sound; the finals are close.

example.pinyin: Tā zài gōngsī hùnle jǐ nián.
example.english: He kicked around the company for a few years.
example.fact: 混 is to mix, and in speech it can also mean to muddle through or hang around: 混日子 (idle away time), 混饭吃 (just get by). 混 is read hún in 混蛋 (scoundrel) and in the sense of 'muddy'.

components.note: 扌 (hand) shows an action.
圭 (guī) gives the sound; the finals are close.

example.fact: 挂 is to hang or to hang up (the phone): 挂电话, 挂号 (register at a hospital), 挂念 (to be concerned). In modern slang 挂了 can mean 'it's dead / crashed' or 'he died'.

components.note: 马 (horse) is the left side, hinting at jumping onto a horse, the original sense.
扁 (biǎn) gives the sound; the finals are close.

example.pinyin: Tā piànle wǒ hěn duō qián.
example.english: He cheated me out of a lot of money.
example.fact: 骗 is to deceive, and gives 骗子 (swindler), 受骗 (be cheated) and 欺骗 (deceive). In the sense of tricking someone it takes the person as the object: 骗他.

components.note: 木 (wood) shows that it was a wooden table.
安 (ān) gives the sound exactly.

example.hanzi: 警察正在调查这个案子。
example.english: The police are investigating this case.
example.fact: 案 means a case (案子, 案件), a record (档案) and a plan or proposal (方案). The original sense was a long table or desk, as in 书案, which still appears in 拍案叫绝 ('slap the table in admiration').

meanings: measure word for long thin things

components.note: 木 (tree) shows the plant.
艮 (gèn) gives the sound; the finals are the same.

example.pinyin: Zhè kē shù de gēn hěn shēn.
example.english: The roots of this tree are deep.
example.fact: 根 is the root of a plant and also a measure word for slender things: 一根筷子 (a chopstick), 一根线 (a thread). It also forms 根本 (fundamental) and 根据 (according to).
